dedupe_keys.name: erncip thematic group deliverables on testing and certification for critical infrastructure security jrc

description: The European Reference Network for Critical Infrastructure Protection (ERNCIP), run by the European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC), organises thematic groups of experts that prepare reports and recommendations on testing, standards and certification for the security of critical infrastructure, sponsored by the Commission and member states. Its site lists twelve thematic groups: chemical and biological risks to drinking water (Austrian Environment Agency), detection of explosives and weapons at secure locations, detection of indoor airborne chemical-biological agents, extended virtual fencing, an industrial automation and control systems (IACS) cybersecurity certification framework (Thales), radiological and nuclear threats to critical infrastructure, resistance of structures to explosion effects (Fraunhofer EMI), and completed groups on biometrics, aviation and non-aviation explosives detection equipment, IACS and smart grids (TNO) and video surveillance. Deliverables listed include a Water Security Plan implementation manual for drinking water systems (January 2022), recommendations for an IACS components cybersecurity certification scheme (September 2020), requirements for robotic equipment carrying radiological and nuclear detectors (April 2022) and a report on dispersion modelling for detecting airborne agents (September 2022). Coverage: EU. Format and access: downloadable reports; free. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-4.0 unless otherwise indicated (European Commission reuse policy). Caveats: the newest deliverable listed is from 2022 and the news items from 2017, so the network may be inactive; the reports were not opened. Simulation uses: threat scenarios, test requirements and security plans for water, energy control systems and buildings, as input to security and cyber-physical resilience studies.
